snip.t: First-line drugs are thiazides, ACE inhibitors or ARBs, and calcium channel blockers.
snip.s: Junior Clerkship in Internal Medicine (MBIM4100) main exam, Paper One: 31 Januar

snip.t: In people of African descent without diabetes or heart failure, a calcium channel blocker or a thiazide-like diuretic is usually more effective first line than an ACE inhibitor or ARB.

Stable narrow-complex irregular tachycardia (AF/Aflutter): Rate control is preferred acutely using intravenous beta-blockers (e.g., metoprolol) or non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (e.g., diltiazem, verapamil).
Use non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (verapamil) if beta-blockers fail or are contraindicated.
Calcium channel blockers: ethosuximide blocks T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons, which controls absence seizures.
snip.s: Clinical Pharmacology I (MBPL 4400) main exam: 25 January 2023

snip.t: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers can worsen reduced ejection fraction.
Avoid NSAIDs, and be careful with fluids and with some calcium channel blockers.
